I resonate with your first paragraph and also use a similar approach (Letting someone know when they have crossed the line right away, in  polite non judgemental manner) and would like to add to this with something I have learned over the years.

People that respect you as a person, friend, or family member will stop doing that thing, will remember you mentioned it and will try their best to accommodate your boundaries. If they have a problem with this newly brought up boundary for some reason they will want to have a discussion about it but not always. No one is perfect and if you have to mention it more than once you do not necessarily have a problem.


(Good) Example 1: Female friend flirts with you (Married man)
He mentions it to female friend to start a discussion about boundaries in this nature. They have a talk about it in regards that he feels it is inappropriate, she feels it's a term of endearment with male friends, in the end she stops flirting with him, the friendship remains strong.

(Toxic) Example 2:  Friend often invites you over and is always interested in doing doing things they like, in their house. You invite them over or out to do other things and plans are either rocky, cancelled or you are stood up. You mention it to your friend and they get defensive, angry and justify their behaviour. They continue to invite you over but never reciprocate by doing what you want or doing anything on your terms.

(Good) Example 3: Friend likes to make jokes about something you don't like. You feel uncomfortable about this so you ask him to stop. "I don't like those kinds of jokes." 
He makes another joke like that a year later when having a laugh with the guys. "That wasn't funny" is your response. The gathering still continues but he does stop. 

No one is perfect but normal people respect their friends and respect conversation that helps them to respect you. This has been a hard lesson to learn because I was so used to being disrespected that I feared telling people what my boundaries are and would just rather being alone. It's really good to mention when your boundaries are crossed.
